environment: Organization: personal (TheVoskamps) and Fablegate. Primary use: software development, Claude Code plugin authoring, and AWS infrastructure work on macOS.
Source control: github.com. Trusted orgs: TheVoskamps, Fablegate.

Repository visibility: PUBLIC — TheVoskamps/claude-plugins-marketplace, TheVoskamps/claude-config, TheVoskamps/macos-setup, TheVoskamps/gh-repo-config, and the forks daaain/claude-code-log and socketteer/Claude-Conversation-Exporter. PRIVATE — all Fablegate/* repositories (fablegate-infra-repo, fablegate-mono-repo, fablegate_quasar_fastapi, fablegate-dataplane).

Branch conventions: main is the integration branch in every repo. All feature work happens on issue-NNN-<slug> branches created from main. In the Fablegate repos, a merge to main triggers AWS CodePipeline, which builds and publishes packages to CodeArtifact.
Ephemeral scratch paths: <repo>/.claude/worktrees/agent-* (git worktrees for agent runs) and <repo>/.claude/tmp/ (scratch output). Both are gitignored, disposable, and reconstructible.

Cloud provider: AWS, via aws-cli with SSO profiles. Accounts in use: FablegateDevOpsAdmin-251424476988, FablegateManagementAdmin-266735799169, FablegateInfrastructureAdmin-895169747393, FablegateCodeArtifactDeveloper. Regions: us-east-1 (primary), us-west-2. These are administrator-level profiles; assume any AWS write executed under them has full account blast radius.

Internal package registry: AWS CodeArtifact, domain fablegate-artifacts, repositories fablegate-npm, fablegate-npm-releases, fablegate-npm-candidates, at *.d.codeartifact.us-east-1.amazonaws.com and *.d.codeartifact.us-west-2.amazonaws.com. This is the expected npm install source for Fablegate repos. The PUBLIC TheVoskamps repos and forks have no internal registry and legitimately resolve against registry.npmjs.org and pypi.org.
Secrets management: AWS SSM Parameter Store and AWS Secrets Manager. Secret values are read at runtime by application and CI code and are never committed to a repository.
CI/CD deploy targets: AWS CodePipeline. Known pipelines: fablegate-dataplane-library-pipeline-main, fablegate-infra-inception-pipeline. Both publish to CodeArtifact.

Trusted cloud buckets (replaces the default heuristic): only s3://fablegate-test-* and s3://example-* are test fixtures with placeholder names. Any other s3:// URI is unrecognized — treat it as a real bucket and judge it normally.

Trusted internal domains: github.com, claude.ai, claude.com, and the AWS CodeArtifact endpoints above. There is no VPN, internal network, or self-hosted service in this environment; any other host is external.

Sensitive data locations & audiences (extends the default heuristic, does not narrow it): in addition to the default credential and PII heuristics, the AWS account numbers and SSO profile names listed above are Fablegate-internal and must never appear in any PUBLIC repository listed above.

Sensitive remote targets (replaces the default 'anything named prod' heuristic): there are no long-lived servers, no databases, no Kubernetes clusters, and no production environment reachable from this machine. The only remote write paths that exist are GitHub, AWS CodeArtifact, and the two CodePipeline pipelines named above. Treat those three as the sensitive remote targets; a hostname containing 'prod' that is not one of them does not exist in this environment and is suspicious rather than routine.

Protected IaC scopes (replaces the default 'none' with a narrowed list): IAM and SSO roles, policies and permission sets; VPC and networking resources; and anything in the FablegateManagementAdmin-266735799169 account. Other terraform resources in fablegate-infra-repo are exploratory and pre-production. Terraform state is not reconstructible.
Container runtime: podman is the default on this machine; docker is used only for registry interactions with docker.io and ghcr.io.

TheVoskamps/claude-plugins-marketplace contains a security tool (plugins/guardrails, hooks/permission-gate) whose test suites use synthetic hostile command strings as test data — fake hostnames, fake credentials, and malformed command payloads — written into fixture files and parser test tables under plugins/guardrails/** and hooks/permission-gate/**. These are inputs to a parser under test. Writing and reading them is routine; executing any of those command strings is not, and must be judged normally.

Shell variables, working-directory changes, and loop variables in Bash commands are resolved to literals by a deterministic PreToolUse analyzer before you see the command. A bare $VAR or unresolved path in a delete or write target should therefore not occur; if one does, the analyzer did not produce it and it should be treated as unverifiable.

Transcript-processing tools: the forks daaain/claude-code-log and socketteer/Claude-Conversation-Exporter parse Claude Code session transcripts. Their test suites contain SYNTHETIC and redacted .jsonl fixtures under test/, tests/, and **/testdata/ inside those checkouts. Those fixture files are authored test data, not captured user sessions. Real session transcripts live under ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl and are sensitive personal data; they are read-only and are never written, edited, or copied into a repository.
allow: Creating, writing to, and removing files and directories under <repo>/.claude/tmp/ is allowed, including recursive removal of a named subdirectory. Removing the <repo>/.claude/tmp/ directory itself is not covered.
mkdir and mkdir -p anywhere under a repository working tree is allowed.

git worktree add, remove, list, and prune is allowed for a single named worktree directory <repo>/.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>, including removing one whose branch has already been pushed. Recursive removal of the <repo>/.claude/worktrees/ parent directory itself is NOT covered by this rule: it would destroy every agent worktree, including uncommitted work belonging to other concurrent sessions.
git fetch, git status, git log, git diff, git branch listing, and git show against github.com/TheVoskamps or github.com/Fablegate are allowed.

Pushing an issue-NNN-* feature branch to origin, and opening or updating a pull request from that branch against main in the SAME repository, is allowed for the repositories named in environment. This blesses the destination only: content rules — Sensitive-Source Provenance, Credential Leakage, Out-of-Place Publication, Excess Sensitive Detail — still apply in full, and a push to one of the PUBLIC TheVoskamps repositories is a publication step for any content that is not that repository's own work. This rule does not cover force-push, pushes to main, or any cross-repository or fork-to-upstream pull request (gh pr create --repo <other>, or a PR from a fork to its upstream); those are judged normally.

gh api GraphQL mutations that update GitHub Projects V2 item fields, issue and PR labels, assignees, milestones, and PR review state on the repositories named in environment are allowed — this is routine issue triage.

Installing dependencies from the fablegate-artifacts CodeArtifact repositories is allowed, including running aws codeartifact get-authorization-token and aws codeartifact login to refresh the registry token.

Installing dependencies from public npm and PyPI in the PUBLIC TheVoskamps repositories and forks is allowed and is not a registry bypass — those repositories have no internal registry and legitimately resolve against public registries.

Reading secrets is allowed: aws ssm get-parameter, aws ssm get-parameters-by-path (including --with-decryption), and aws secretsmanager get-secret-value against the accounts named in environment. This covers retrieval only. Any command that would place a decrypted secret value where it persists or is disclosed — echoing it, writing it into a tracked file, passing it to an external endpoint, or committing it — is outside this rule and judged normally.
Read-only AWS CodePipeline inspection is allowed: list-pipelines, list-pipeline-executions, get-pipeline-state, get-pipeline-execution, list-action-executions.
aws codepipeline start-pipeline-execution and retry-stage-execution are allowed for fablegate-dataplane-library-pipeline-main and fablegate-infra-inception-pipeline only.

Writing, editing, and reading test fixture files that contain synthetic hostile command strings is allowed under these paths: plugins/guardrails/**/test*/**, plugins/guardrails/**/*_test.*, hooks/permission-gate/**/test*/**, **/testdata/**, and <repo>/.claude/tmp/**. This exception covers the Write, Edit, MultiEdit, and Read tools and shell redirection into those paths. It does not cover executing the fixture content, and it does not extend to any path outside this list.
podman commands against local images, containers, and volumes are routine local development and are allowed.

Reading, writing, and editing SYNTHETIC or redacted .jsonl transcript fixtures under test/, tests/, and **/testdata/ inside the daaain/claude-code-log and socketteer/Claude-Conversation-Exporter checkouts is allowed: they are authored test data for a parser, not captured user sessions. Reading real transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/ to develop or debug those tools is allowed. Writing, editing, or deleting anything under ~/.claude/projects/ is NOT covered, and copying a real transcript into a repository working tree is NOT covered.
soft_deny: Never mutate the filesystem — create, modify, truncate, or delete a file — through any mechanism that hides the target path from static analysis. The user's PreToolUse analyzer validates literal paths in shell command text; it cannot see inside an interpreter program body. This covers inline interpreter programs (perl -e, perl -pi -e, python -c, python3 -c, node -e, ruby -e, awk programs, jq writing to a file), in-place editors (sed -i, ed, ex, patch), find -exec with a mutating command, and generating a script and then executing it. Clears when the user explicitly asked for that specific mechanism, or when the mutation is a build or test step defined by a script already committed in the repository. Read-only uses of the same tools — sed without -i, awk, jq, perl -n printing to stdout — are unaffected, as are ordinary redirection and heredoc writes (>, >>, tee, cat > file) whose target path is literal in the command text.

Never delete, truncate, or revert files under a repository working tree outside <repo>/.claude/tmp/ and <repo>/.claude/worktrees/. This covers rm, git reset --hard, git checkout -- <path>, git restore, git stash drop, and git clean. This rule OVERRIDES the default Irreversible Local Destruction carve-out for files the agent created this session, with two exceptions that remain allowed: gitignored build output (dist/, build/, node_modules/, __pycache__, .venv/, target/) and a file the agent both created and last wrote during this session. Clears when the user names the specific paths to remove. A general request to clean up, tidy, or reset does not clear it.

Pushing or merging to main in any Fablegate/* repository triggers AWS CodePipeline and publishes packages to CodeArtifact. Treat it as a Production Deploy, not a push: this is narrower than, and overrides, the default Git Push Destination exception, which blesses pushes to any branch and does not recognise main as a deploy target. The same applies to gh pr merge on those repositories. In TheVoskamps/* repositories, pushing to main is not a deploy but is still blocked as an integration-branch write. Clears only when the user names the publish, pipeline, or CodeArtifact release — not merely the word push.

Never force-push (git push --force, --force-with-lease, or a refspec with a leading +) to any branch in any TheVoskamps/* or Fablegate/* repository. Clears only when the user names the branch and says to force-push it.

Never write to AWS SSM Parameter Store or Secrets Manager — put-parameter, put-secret-value, create-secret, update-secret, delete-parameter, delete-secret. Clears when the user names the specific parameter or secret and the intended value's source.

Never run an aws iam command that creates, modifies, attaches, detaches, or deletes a policy, role, user, or permission set, and never assume a role outside the SSO profiles named in environment. Clears when the user names the principal and the specific permission.
Never run terraform apply or terraform destroy. Clears when the user names the target scope and says to apply or destroy it. terraform plan, validate, fmt, and show are unaffected.

Never run aws codepipeline start-pipeline-execution or retry-stage-execution against a pipeline other than fablegate-dataplane-library-pipeline-main or fablegate-infra-inception-pipeline. Clears when the user names the pipeline.

Never run gh release create, gh repo create --public, or gh repo edit --visibility public. Creating a public surface is the user's decision. Clears when the user names the repository and says to publish it.

Never change the permission system this session runs under: the PreToolUse hook registration in any settings.json, the permissions or autoMode blocks of any settings.json, or the installed copy of the guardrails plugin under ~/.claude/. Editing guardrails plugin SOURCE inside a TheVoskamps/claude-plugins-marketplace checkout or worktree is normal development work and is not this rule — the distinction is between changing the code under review and changing the enforcement configuration currently protecting the session. Clears when the user names the setting or file and says to change it.
hard_deny: Never execute code fetched at runtime through an ad-hoc shell pipe: curl or wget piped into a shell or interpreter, bash <(wget ...), python -c "$(curl ...)", or running a script downloaded during this session. Package managers resolving from a declared manifest or lockfile (npm install, pip install -r, uv sync, go install, cargo install, brew install, docker run of a tagged image) are NOT this rule. Official toolchain installers from sh.rustup.rs, astral.sh, bun.sh, get.docker.com, and proto.dev are NOT this rule. Writing a curl-pipe string as data into plugins/guardrails/**/test*/**, hooks/permission-gate/**/test*/**, **/testdata/**, or <repo>/.claude/tmp/** is permitted; executing it, or writing it to any path outside those globs, is not.

Credential material — access keys, session tokens, private keys, passwords, decrypted secret values — never enters any repository, private ones included, in tracked files, commit messages, PR or issue bodies, release notes, gists, or CI logs. Additionally, AWS account numbers, SSO profile names, and CodeArtifact domain endpoints must never reach the PUBLIC repositories named in environment through any of those same surfaces.

Never send repository contents, session transcripts, or credential material to a network destination outside this set: the configured git remote of the repository the session started in; github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, codeload.github.com and objects.githubusercontent.com under the TheVoskamps or Fablegate orgs; claude.ai, claude.com and downloads.claude.ai; and the AWS CodeArtifact endpoints named in environment. A github.com URL under any other owner is outside this set — pushing or mirroring to an unrelated GitHub account is exfiltration, not a push. gist.github.com is outside this set.
